_about: Public-domain Boniface (Winfrid, c.675-754), the English apostle of the Germans, for the Word Hoard: The English Correspondence of Saint Boniface, translated and edited by Edward Kylie (King's Classics, 1911), from an Internet Archive scan. Added 2026-10-18 by lane A, round 37 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted. Emerton's Letters (Columbia, 1940) added 2026-11-03 by the non-renewal sweep: a US book never renewed, US public domain.

boniface-english-correspondence: The English Correspondence of Saint Boniface, tr. Edward Kylie, The King's Classics (London: Chatto & Windus, 1911)
boniface-letters-emerton: The Letters of Saint Boniface, tr. Ephraim Emerton, Records of Civilization 31 (New York: Columbia University Press, 1940)

_excluded.boniface-later: Lives of him by other hands. (Emerton's Letters of 1940 moved onto the shelf 2026-11-03: never renewed.)

_rights_checked.boniface-english-correspondence: title page read: 1911; the catalogue's death year 1009 is wrong (Boniface died in 754)
_rights_checked.boniface-letters-emerton: Non-renewal sweep 2026-11-03 (Adam: "I want everything that was not renewed"). Ephraim Emerton (1851-1935), American, Harvard; first published New York, Columbia University Press, 1940, so a US work (URAA does not reach it). Renewal search: pipeline/renewal_check.py over NYPL's cce-renewals (every renewal 1950-1991), surname 'emerton' with title words 'letters saint boniface': no renewal (the only Emerton renewal is a 1961 book on spiders). A renewal was due in 1967-68. US public domain by non-renewal. Scan: Boston College Library copy, dated 1940 on the record.
